quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.
Use both brakes every time.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes every time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What about the front brake?

options.text: Use it only when you need to stop quickly.
Use it only on slippery roads.
It is less effective than the rear brake.
It is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is safe to use when used correctly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It is safe to use both brakes any time you slow or stop, as long as you use the front brake properly.

questions.question: What is a properly-fitted motorcycle?

options.text: One where your feet can touch the ground while you are seated.
One with a seat at your waist level.
One with a seat 10 inches above your waist.
One with a seat 10 inches below your waist.

questions.correctAnswerText: One where your feet can touch the ground while you are seated.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle fits properly if your feet can reach the ground while sitting on the seat. When riding, keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Your motorcycle begins to weave while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Brake suddenly.
Steer in a weaving pattern.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and go straight at a steady speed. Weaving to match the motorcycle's movement will make things worse.

questions.question: When riding in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlight.
Low beam headlight.
No lights.
Switch between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: When it starts raining, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane when it is wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by other cars. The left tire track is often best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, if traffic is heavy.
Yes, during the day to prevent traffic jams.
Yes, if the rider is comfortable doing it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: How should you brake?

options.text: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
Grab at the front brake and squeeze the rear brake.
Jam on the front brake and grab at the rear brake.
Press down on the front brake and jam on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the front brake and press the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the front brake lever and press down on the rear brake pedal. Always use both brakes when you slow or stop.

questions.question: What should your lane position accomplish?

options.text: Protect your lane from other drivers.
Give you a nice view of scenery.
Place you in other drivers' blind spots.
Hide your plans from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect your lane from other drivers.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should keep you out of blind spots, help you see and be seen, avoid road hazards, avoid wind blasts, and give you an escape route. Position yourself to prevent other drivers from trying to share your lane.

questions.question: As you slow down or stop, what should you do with the gears?

options.text: Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.
Take the bike out of gear.
Stay in the same gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, where should you position yourself in the lane?

options.text: Always stay away from the left side of the lane.
Always stay away from the right side of the lane.
Always stay away from the center of the lane.
Use whatever part of the lane is safest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use whatever part of the lane is safest.
questions.explanation: There is no single lane position you must always avoid. Change your position based on road conditions.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes to stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. Brake slowly on the good tire only. Move to the side of the road as you slow down, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Why should you check your mirrors when stopped at an intersection?

options.text: To see if parked cars are entering traffic.
To see if vehicles are changing lanes.
To watch for vehicles behind you that may not stop in time.
To see if someone is turning behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for vehicles behind you that may not stop in time.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, check your mirrors for cars approaching from behind. Drivers may not see you until it is too late, so you may need to react quickly.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
A high load may block your vision.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: Placing a load too high on a motorcycle raises its center of gravity and makes it harder to balance.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop if a tire goes flat while you are riding?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle while staying straight. Brake slowly on the good tire only. Move toward the road edge as you slow down, pull in the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Keep you hidden from other drivers.
Help other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you hidden from other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen, keeps you out of blind spots, avoids hazards, shows your intentions, protects you from wind, and gives you an escape route. You should never want to stay hidden from other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
Signal and check your mirrors.
Look over your shoulder and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Use your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check for traffic around you.

questions.question: A good eye or face shield should have all of these features except:

options.text: Free of scratches
Hard to break through
Fastens securely
Airtight

questions.correctAnswerText: Airtight
questions.explanation: Good eye protection must be scratch-free, hard to break, fasten securely, have clear side vision, allow air to pass through, and fit over glasses. It should not be airtight.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Where is the rear brake pedal located on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handlebar grip
On the right handlebar grip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right footrest
questions.explanation: The rear brake pedal is usually located near the right footrest on a motorcycle.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are white with black lettering. They show rules like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean when the operator leans.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when they lean. Hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt. Sit as close to the operator as you can without crowding them.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Keep your normal following distance.
Brake later than normal.
Ride slower than normal.
Ride faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Ride slower, especially through curves and over bumps. Your motorcycle will take longer to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep more distance between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, tell them to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before you ride. Have them get on only after you start the engine. They should sit as close as possible without crowding you and hold your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep both feet on the footrests at all times.

questions.question: On a motorcycle:

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake.
The emergency brake is more powerful than both.
Use only one brake at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake does most of the stopping. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Always use both brakes at the same time when slowing or stopping.
